Selling a Maine House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Maine statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Maine property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Written abatement application to the assessors must be filed within 185 days from commitment; assessors may also abate on their own initiative within one year. (36 M.R.S. §841(1); source)
  • After one year but within 3 years from commitment, the municipal officers may abate for illegality, error or irregularity, but may not grant an abatement to correct an error in valuation. (36 M.R.S. §841(1); source)
  • If a municipality has a board of assessment review, an applicant denied abatement may appeal in writing to it within 60 days after notice of the decision or deemed denial. (36 M.R.S. §843(1); source)
  • Residential appeals from the board of assessment review go directly to Superior Court under Rule 80B; nonresidential property or property with equalized municipal valuation of $1,000,000 or greater goes to the State Board of Property Tax Review within 60 days. (36 M.R.S. §843(1), (1-A); source)
  • A taxpayer filing an appeal must pay the greater of the prior year's taxes (up to current taxes due) or the undisputed current taxes; this does not apply to property valued under $500,000. (36 M.R.S. §843(4); source)
  • 'Certified ratio' is the level of assessed value, as a percentage of just value, as certified by the assessor under 36 M.R.S. §383. (Maine Revenue Services Property Tax Bulletin 31; source)
  • Maine uses a tax lien mortgage rather than a tax sale: if unpaid within 18 months after filing the certificate, the mortgage is deemed foreclosed and redemption expires. (36 M.R.S. §943; source)
  • The treasurer must notify the owner and mortgage holders 30 to 45 days before the foreclosure date. (36 M.R.S. §943; source)
Selling in Maine?
We buy Maine houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Details we could not confirm on an official page are not stated.

How to sell a Maine house when this applies to you

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Maine.

What a cash sale of a Maine house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Maine.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Maine disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Maine

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Maine change, so confirm details with the official office or a Maine attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Maine

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

What happens to unpaid property tax when I sell?

The closing agent pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds at closing.

  • A permanent resident who loses a homestead to tax lien foreclosure and regains it from the municipality is deemed to have continuously owned it. (36 M.R.S. §683(1); source)

Maine Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House

Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Maine statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Maine evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Tenancies at will terminate by at least 30 days' written notice from either party. (14 M.R.S. §6002(1); source)
  • A 7-day written notice is available for grounds including 7 or more days of rent arrears, nuisance, substantial damage or unauthorized occupant. (14 M.R.S. §6002(2); source)
  • Paying full rent due before a 7-day arrears notice expires voids it; paying all arrears and fees before the writ issues reinstates the tenancy. (14 M.R.S. §6002; source)
  • The court issues the writ of possession 7 calendar days after judgment; a sheriff or constable may serve it. (14 M.R.S. §6005; source)
  • On sale of a rental, the person holding security deposits must account for and transfer them to the successor, and notify tenants by mail. (14 M.R.S. §6035; source)
  • When the landlord's interest ends by sale, the accounting and transfer must occur no later than the real estate closing, with written proof given to the buyer. (14 M.R.S. §6035; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Maine statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Maine probate runs through the courts named in the sources below. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Collection of personal property by affidavit requires the value of the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, not to exceed $40,000 (inflation-adjusted) and 30 days elapsed since death. (18-C M.R.S. §3-1201; source)
  • Section 3-1201 is titled Collection of personal property by affidavit; it does not by its title transfer real estate. (18-C M.R.S. §3-1201; source)
  • A personal representative may not sell or transfer estate real property without 10 days' prior notice to persons succeeding to an interest, unless the will authorizes sale without notice. (18-C M.R.S. §3-711; source)
  • Deeds of distribution under Title 18-C are exempt from the real estate transfer tax. (36 M.R.S. §4641-C(11); source)
